/salkantay-treks/.q: How hard is the Salkantay trek compared to the Inca Trail?
/salkantay-treks/.a: Salkantay reaches higher altitude (up to ~4,630 m / 15,190 ft) and involves longer hiking days than the Classic Inca Trail. It does not require Inca Trail permits. We match you to 4D or 5D routes based on fitness and acclimatization — message us on WhatsApp with your travel month.

/salkantay-treks/.q: When is the best time for Salkantay?
/salkantay-treks/.a: May through September is the dry season with the most reliable trekking weather. Shoulder months (April, October) can work with fewer crowds. We include camping gear and meals on our packages; you bring layers for cold nights at altitude.

/salkantay-treks/.q: Do Salkantay packages include Machu Picchu entry?
/salkantay-treks/.a: Yes — our Salkantay treks end with a guided Machu Picchu visit. Circuit and train tickets depend on your package tier; we confirm availability when you request a quote for your dates.

/luxury-tours/.q: What makes a Peru Grand Travel luxury tour different?
/luxury-tours/.a: Private guides, upgraded hotels (4–5*), Belmond or similar train options where available, and flexible pacing. We design around your interests rather than fixed group departures — share your dates and hotel preferences on WhatsApp.

/luxury-tours/.q: Can you combine luxury stays with trekking?
/luxury-tours/.a: Yes. Many travelers acclimatize in Cusco with boutique hotels, trek Salkantay or take the Sacred Valley, then finish with a premium Machu Picchu visit. We balance comfort with altitude safety.

/luxury-tours/.q: Are Belmond trains and lodges included in listed prices?
/luxury-tours/.a: Belmond and other premium add-ons are often quote-only because availability and season affect cost. Message us for a tailored luxury proposal — no booking fee to ask.

/day-tours-in-cusco/.q: Do day tours include hotel pickup in Cusco?
/day-tours-in-cusco/.a: Most Sacred Valley and Cusco city day tours include pickup from central hotels. Remote lodges may need a meeting point — we confirm when you book for your dates.

/day-tours-in-cusco/.q: Can I combine two day tours in one day?
/day-tours-in-cusco/.a: Some combinations work (e.g. city tour morning + nearby ruins), but altitude and drive times matter. Tell us your must-sees on WhatsApp and we suggest a realistic daily plan.

/day-tours-in-cusco/.q: Do I need the Tourist Ticket (boleto) for day tours?
/day-tours-in-cusco/.a: Many archaeological sites require the Cusco Tourist Ticket or partial tickets. Our tour descriptions note what's included; we clarify extras when quoting your specific day tours.

/offers/.q: How do Peru Grand Travel offers work?
/offers/.a: Offers reflect seasonal promotions or limited departure windows. Prices and inclusions can change — message us on WhatsApp with your travel dates and we'll confirm what's available and lock in the best rate.

/offers/.q: Can I combine an offer with a custom extension?
/offers/.a: Often yes. Many travelers book a promoted package and add Amazon, Lake Titicaca, or extra nights in Lima. We quote the full itinerary so you see one clear total.

/tailor-made-tour/.q: How does a tailor-made Peru itinerary work?
/tailor-made-tour/.a: You share dates, group size, interests, and budget on WhatsApp or email. We reply with 2–3 day-by-day drafts at no obligation. Once you approve, we handle hotels, guides, trains, and permits.

/tailor-made-tour/.q: Is there a minimum trip length for custom tours?
/tailor-made-tour/.a: No strict minimum, but altitude and distances mean most custom routes are 5–14 days. Shorter trips focus on one region (e.g. Cusco + Machu Picchu); longer trips add Lima, Amazon, or the south coast.

/tailor-made-tour/.q: How far in advance should I plan a custom trip?
/tailor-made-tour/.a: For peak season (June–August) and Inca Trail permits, 4–6 months ahead is ideal. Other routes can often be arranged with less notice — contact us and we'll check availability.

/destinations/.q: Which Peru destinations should I combine in one trip?
/destinations/.a: Classic first-timer routes pair Lima, Cusco, Sacred Valley, and Machu Picchu (7–10 days). Add Puno and Lake Titicaca, Arequipa and Colca Canyon, or the Amazon for 12–16 days. We help prioritize based on your time and interests.

/destinations/.q: Do I need to fly between regions?
/destinations/.a: Lima–Cusco and Lima–Arequipa are common domestic flights (1–1.5 hours). Buses work for budget travelers on longer legs. Our packages include recommended transfers — ask us to compare flight vs bus for your dates.

/travel-styles/.q: How do I choose the right travel style for Peru?
/travel-styles/.a: Adventure travelers often pick treks (Inca Trail, Salkantay). Culture-focused trips emphasize Cusco, Sacred Valley ruins, and local food. Families need gentler pacing and kid-friendly hotels — tell us your group on WhatsApp and we filter packages accordingly.

/travel-styles/.q: Can one trip mix adventure and relaxation?
/travel-styles/.a: Yes. A popular pattern is trekking mid-trip with spa or luxury hotel nights before and after. We balance activity days with rest for altitude recovery.
